title: TensorFlow Model Serving in Connect is deprecated
description:
TensorFlow Model serving in Connect is deprecated as of the September 2022 edition release. Support will be removed in a future release. We're recommending folks use an API framework like [Plumber](https://tensorflow.rstudio.com/guides/deploy/plumber), Flask, or FastAPI to create an HTTP API for hosting TensorFlow models on Connect going forward.

https://docs.rstudio.com/connect/user/tensorflow/
https://docs.rstudio.com/connect/news/#rstudio-connect-2022090

title: Move `master` branch to `main`
description:
Cc @t-kalinowski

The `master` branch of this repository will soon be renamed to `main`, as part of a coordinated change across several GitHub organizations (including, but not limited to: [tidyverse](https://github.com/tidyverse), [r-lib](https://github.com/r-lib), [tidymodels](https://github.com/tidymodels), and [sol-eng](https://github.com/sol-eng)). We anticipate this will happen by the end of September 2021.

That will be preceded by a release of the [usethis package](https://usethis.r-lib.org), which will gain some functionality around detecting and adapting to a renamed default branch. There will also be a blog post at the time of this `master` --> `main` change.

The purpose of this issue is to:

* Help us firm up the list of targetted repositories
* Make sure all maintainers are aware of what's coming
* Give us an issue to close when the job is done
* Give us a place to put advice for collaborators re: how to adapt

*message id: entire_lizard*

title: export_savedmodel inconsistencies
description:
I noticed that we have some inconsistencies in both documentation and behavior in our `export_savedmodel()` implementations:

1) The tfestimators package has an `export_dir_base` argument which is documented as "A string containing a directory in which to create timestamped subdirectories containing exported SavedModels." This behaves as expected/documented.

2) The tensorflow package has an `export_dir_base` argument (similar to tfestimators). This S3 method includes no documentation and *does not* create timestamped subdirectories.

3) The keras package has an `export_dir_base` argument which is documented to create versioned timestamped subdirectories however it *does not do this* (rather it always writes to the same root directory).

We need to clean up the parameter names, documentation, and behavior. It's fine to keep the timestamped subdirectories for estimators, however if don't do this for keras and tensorflow this parameter should be named `export_dir` and not be documented to created subdirectories. In this case we should also include an `overwrite` parameter to remove the directory before exporting (otherwise we need `unlink()` boilerplate everywhere.

title: Failed to load swagger spec
description:
Hi. I am getting a "failed to load spec." error from the Swagger UI when trying to serve the example model:

```
library(tfdeploy)
model_path <- system.file("models/tensorflow-mnist/", package = "tfdeploy")
serve_savedmodel(model_path)
```

Stepping through the code on my system, I don't think `swagger_from_signature_def` is generating the swagger file. I've been able to verify this error with the following code

```
model_path <- system.file("models/tensorflow-mnist/", package = "tfdeploy")
graph <- with_new_session(function(sess) load_savedmodel(sess, model_path))
signature_def <- graph$signature_def
swagger_from_signature_def(signature_def)
```

My system also fails to pass the `test-serve.R` tests locally. Are these tests passing on other systems or is it just my configuration? Would appreciate any help.
